hl: Double or triple your business with one acquisition.
text: If you own a business doing more than a million dollars a year, give me the next few minutes. I'm going to show you how owners like you are doubling, and in some cases tripling, the size of their business in one move. They do it by buying a competitor. They put none of their own money into the deal. And they get to a signed letter of intent in about ninety days.

hl: Two businesses bought with 100% seller finance.
text: My name is Josh Li. I'm the founder of JC Health Group. When I wanted to grow faster than organic growth would let me, I stopped trying to win one customer at a time, and I bought businesses instead. I've bought two of them. Both were one hundred percent seller financed. So everything I'm about to share with you, I've done myself, in my own businesses, with my own name on the contracts.

Let me guess where you're at right now. You've built something real. It pays well, you've got a team, and you've got customers who trust you. But growth has started to feel heavy. Every new dollar of revenue costs you more marketing, another hire, and more of your own time. You're working in the business when you know you should be working on it. And if you're honest, next year looks a lot like this year. Just a little bigger, and a little more tiring.

Most owners think there are only two ways out of that. The first is to keep grinding. Spend more on ads, hire more people, and hope the numbers move faster than your costs. That works, slowly, and it takes years. The second is to raise money. You bring in investors, give away a piece of the company you built, and now you answer to someone else. There's a third way, and it's the one I use. You buy a business that's already built. Its customers, its team and its profit join yours on day one. And the purchase is paid for by the seller and the bank, out of that business's own cash flow.

hl: Owners are ready to sell. Most never list.
text: Right now, a huge number of business owners are getting ready to retire. Many of them have no succession plan. Their kids don't want the business, and their managers can't afford to buy it. Most of these businesses never go to a broker. They never appear on a listing site. They're waiting for someone to pick up the phone and ask one simple question. Have you ever thought about selling? And when an owner does decide to sell, they rarely pick the highest bidder. They pick the buyer they trust to look after their staff, their customers, and their name.

hl: Your business makes you the credible buyer.
text: This is where you have a massive advantage. You already run a business in the industry. You've got a team, systems, a track record, and profit. To a retiring owner, you're the obvious successor. To a lender, you're a buyer who already knows how to run the asset. First-time buyers spend years trying to build that kind of credibility. You already have it. You just haven't used it yet.

The way we do this is a system I call the three C's. The first C is Capabilities. We put the right people around you, so when you sit down with a seller or a bank, there's serious deal experience in the room. The second C is Capital. We engineer the structure so the seller and the lender fund the purchase, with a buffer built in. And the third C is Closing. You find the deals off market, you control the process, and you get to a signed letter of intent without getting dragged into a broker auction.

Let me show you what that looks like. Say there's a competitor making five hundred thousand dollars a year in profit, and you agree a price of one and a half million. A lender funds most of the price. The seller carries part of it as a note, paid back over time out of the business's profit. And the lender adds a working capital line on top. So you end up with more funding than the price. The extra covers your closing costs, and gives you working capital from day one. The rule we never break is this. The business has to earn about one and a half times what it owes each year. So the deal pays for itself, with a buffer, and it never leans on your existing business. I break that example down, line by line, in part two.

hl: The bank, your time, and the risk.
text: Now, you're probably asking yourself a few questions. Will the bank actually go for this? We line up the financing with you before you sign the letter of intent, so you know the structure works before you commit. Do I have to put my own cash in? No. That's the whole point of the structure. Do I have the time? This is done with you, so you're never on your own. Expect a few focused hours a week, with my team coaching every conversation. And will a second business distract me from the first? It's a real risk. That's why integration planning starts on day one. We help you buy a business your team can absorb, and build the management layer, so the group doesn't depend on you.

Here's how the ninety days work. In weeks one and two, we audit your business with you and set your target profile. That's the business that could double or triple yours. In weeks three to eight, you run outreach to owners, on and off market, using our scripts, while we coach every conversation. And in weeks nine to thirteen, we're in the room as you negotiate. We line up the financing with you, and you sign the letter of intent.

And here's what most owners miss. Larger, more diversified businesses are often valued at a higher multiple of earnings than small ones. So when you buy a business, you're doing two things at once. You're adding its profit to yours. And you're lifting what every dollar of that profit is worth. That's why an acquisition can grow your exit value far faster than organic growth ever could.

So think about what it costs you to stay where you are. Another year of growing one customer at a time. Another year of carrying everything on your own shoulders. Another year where a competitor buys the business you should have bought. Now picture this time next year. Two businesses. Combined profit. A stronger team, and a company that's worth far more than it is today. That's a business that gives you options, and a life that doesn't depend on you working harder.
